Coverage by source of evidence: card, recall and either

Source: R/estimate.R
estimate_coverage_by_evidence.Rd

The standard presentation of a coverage survey reports each antigen three ways: documented on the vaccination card, reported by the caregiver, and either source ("card or recall"). This function derives all three and returns them stacked, labelled by evidence.

estimate_coverage_by_evidence(
  x,
  vaccines = NULL,
  by = NULL,
  evidence = c("card", "recall", "card_or_recall"),
  labels = c("Card", "Recall", "Card or recall"),
  denominator = c("all", "determinable"),
  design_args = list(),
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A vcs_data object with card and recall evidence mapped.

vaccines

Vaccine names. Defaults to every vaccine present.

by

Domains, as a one-sided formula or character vector.

evidence

Evidence definitions to compare, from vcs_evidence_definitions().

labels

Display labels for evidence, same length.

denominator

"all" or "determinable"; see Denominators.

design_args

Arguments passed to vcs_design().

...

Passed to estimate_coverage() (level, deff).

Value

A vcs_estimate tibble with an evidence column, ordered by vaccine then evidence.

Denominators

denominator = "all" (default) follows the convention of most published coverage tables: every enumerated child is in the denominator of every row, and a child with no evidence from a given source counts as not vaccinated by that source. A child with no card is therefore "not documented on the card" – which is true – and the card row reads as documented coverage, not as coverage among card holders. This is missing_as_unvaccinated = TRUE applied explicitly, and the rule is recorded on every derived column.

denominator = "determinable" keeps the package default: a child with no evidence from a source has unknown status for that source and is excluded from that row. Denominators then differ between rows, and the card row becomes coverage among children whose card was seen.

State which convention a table uses. They answer different questions.

See also

estimate_coverage(), derive_vaccination_status()

Examples

est <- estimate_coverage_by_evidence(
  vcs_example, vaccines = c("BCG", "PENTA1", "PENTA3", "MCV1")
)
est[, c("indicator", "evidence", "numerator", "denominator", "estimate")]
#> <vcs_estimate: 12 row(s)>
#>   evidence : card | recall | card_or_recall
#> # A tibble: 12 × 5
#>    indicator evidence       numerator denominator estimate
#>    <chr>     <fct>              <dbl>       <dbl>    <dbl>
#>  1 BCG       Card                 138         256    0.534
#>  2 BCG       Recall               209         256    0.804
#>  3 BCG       Card or recall       218         256    0.843
#>  4 PENTA1    Card                 137         256    0.541
#>  5 PENTA1    Recall               214         256    0.840
#>  6 PENTA1    Card or recall       227         256    0.893
#>  7 PENTA3    Card                  82         256    0.329
#>  8 PENTA3    Recall               130         256    0.513
#>  9 PENTA3    Card or recall       137         256    0.541
#> 10 MCV1      Card                  93         256    0.372
#> 11 MCV1      Recall               145         256    0.578
#> 12 MCV1      Card or recall       151         256    0.601

estimate_coverage_by_evidence(vcs_example, vaccines = "PENTA3", by = ~stratum)
#> <vcs_estimate: 6 row(s)>
#>   evidence : card | recall | card_or_recall
#> # A tibble: 6 × 15
#>   indicator evidence       domain stratum numerator denominator estimate     se
#>   <chr>     <fct>          <chr>  <chr>       <dbl>       <dbl>    <dbl>  <dbl>

#> 2 PENTA3    Recall         rural  rural          51         126    0.412 0.0406
#> 3 PENTA3    Card or recall rural  rural          52         126    0.420 0.0380
#> 4 PENTA3    Card           urban  urban          53         130    0.427 0.0440
#> 5 PENTA3    Recall         urban  urban          79         130    0.612 0.0387
#> 6 PENTA3    Card or recall urban  urban          85         130    0.661 0.0448
#> # ℹ 7 more variables: conf_low <dbl>, conf_high <dbl>, n_unweighted <dbl>,
